source_snapshot.purpose_facts: Set an operator-specified NVIDIA GPU power limit, read it back and verify normal system operation.
procedure_facts: Source command uses typographic dashes, uppercase `I`, unspecified GPU_number and Watts.
Attended and machine time are each five minutes.
criteria_facts: Power limit saves successfully and system works normally.
missing_source_information: Stable GPU scope, target watts, device-supported range, meaning of save/persistence, monitoring limits and restoration value.

original_test_intent.statement: Apply an approved power cap to the selected NVIDIA GPU(s), prove the requested cap is accepted/read back while the system remains healthy, and restore the pre-test state after evidence collection.
must_preserve: Actual power-limit mutation and readback, not inventory only.
Selected GPU scope, approved watts and five-minute test activity.
must_not_infer: That `-pl` persists across driver unload or reboot.
That a successful command proves the enforced cap or system health.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 fixes ASCII syntax, requires GPU/watts/range approval, captures current/default limits, monitors health and restores the recorded limit.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: `USER CONFIRMATION` is not one of the four formal classifications. V2 also asks whether the value persists without defining a reboot/unload test, and its all-GPU readback can misattribute requested versus enforced limit or miss newer GPU/module power scopes.

related_records: Read-only power queries do not authorize this state-changing cap test.
applicable_history.precedence_application: Formal V3 taxonomy controls classification; the source requires a bounded mutation but not reboot-persistence testing.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Normalize V2's noncanonical label. Bind the cap to stable UUID/BDF and explicit supported power scope, verify requested and enforced readback plus health, then restore the exact pre-test setting; do not add a reboot persistence test.

conditions_present: Driver tool and bounded five-minute set/readback intent.
missing: GPU UUID/BDF, GPU-versus-module scope, watts/range, original/restoration value, workload drain, health limits and approval.
provider: Platform/workload owner supplies target/scope/watts and maintenance approval.
GPU owner supplies supported range/scope and restoration rule.
safe_read_only_work: Collect GPU UUID/BDF/model, driver help/version, supported/current/requested/enforced/default/min/max power values, active processes, telemetry and logs.
prohibited_until_resolved: Any `-pl` mutation, broad all-GPU selection, reboot/unload, workload interference, auto-retry or PASS.
closure_evidence: Signed GPU/scope/watts/restoration tuple within reported range and guarded window.

revision_candidate.test_name: Set, Verify and Restore NVIDIA GPU Power Limit
revision_candidate.purpose: Set the approved power limit on each explicitly selected NVIDIA GPU power scope, verify requested and enforced readback against the owner-defined relationship while the system remains healthy, and restore the exact recorded pre-test limit without adding a reboot-persistence test.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Exact NVIDIA GPU/server and installed driver where `nvidia-smi` reports the selected GPU or module power scope and supports power-limit setting.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Only approved stable GPU UUIDs or PCI BDFs and the explicitly selected GPU/module/base-power scope. Perform one bounded set/readback/health/restore sequence; enumeration indexes alone are not stable scope. The source's five minutes is a planning estimate for the complete activity, not a required dwell, maximum timeout or acceptance criterion.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Stable UUID/BDF list; target watts and intended power scope; current/requested/enforced/default/min/max values; signed rule or tolerance for the expected requested-versus-enforced relationship; driver-specific supported syntax; workload drain; thermal/power/performance health thresholds; original-value restoration plan; privileged access, maintenance and OOB approval.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: First collect identity, active workloads, all supported power-limit properties, telemetry and health. Validate the requested watts against the reported range and the signed requested-versus-enforced rule for the exact scope. After approval, use the driver-supported ASCII `nvidia-smi -i <approved_UUID_or_BDF> -pl <watts>` plus any explicitly required scope option. Capture command status, then query the same stable targets for requested/current/enforced limit and telemetry; evaluate both values against the signed relationship/tolerance without inventing a dwell. Restore each recorded pre-test value, verify requested/enforced restoration under the same rule and final health. Do not reboot or unload the driver unless a separate persistence test is authorized.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Targets idle/drained; stable IDs and scope proven; values in supported range; requested/enforced rule, privilege, telemetry, recovery and restoration available; approval recorded.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Host/driver/GPU model/UUID/BDF; command help/scope support; selected targets/scope/watts and approval; source five-minute planning estimate; signed requested-versus-enforced relationship/tolerance; pre requested/enforced/default/min/max limits; exact set/readback/restore commands/statuses; target-correlated requested/enforced values and evaluated deltas; power/temperature/clock/throttle telemetry; workload status; XID/dmesg/BMC/SEL deltas; final restored values and health.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Owner-approved target/scope/watts within device-reported limits and its signed requested-versus-enforced rule. Complete when every selected target's requested value equals the approved setting, its enforced/current value satisfies the declared relationship/tolerance, health remains acceptable, and both limit state and platform return to the exact approved pre-test condition. Five minutes is planning metadata, and no reboot persistence is implied.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not infer index/watts/scope, use typographic options, set all GPUs unintentionally, exceed range, change clocks/firmware, run against active workloads, conflate requested with enforced power, omit restoration, reboot to test persistence, or continue after health/restoration failure.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Explicit approval for GPU list, power scope, watts, workload impact, privileged mutation and restoration; engineer judges telemetry/performance and any limit mismatch.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: The agent may perform the exact guarded set/readback/restore; scope/value choice and anomaly disposition are human decisions.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On rejection, target mismatch, thermal/power/XID/workload anomaly or readback discrepancy, stop further targets, preserve evidence, restore every changed target to its recorded pre-state and verify health; use OOB/vendor recovery if the driver is unavailable.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unknown stable target/scope/range/pre-state; active workload; absent approval/telemetry/recovery; unsupported syntax; set/readback mismatch; thermal/power/throttle/XID error; driver loss; restoration failure; incomplete evidence.

identified_defects: Source syntax and target/watts are invalid placeholders.
Requested/enforced and GPU/module power scopes are not distinguished.
Persistence beyond immediate readback is undefined.
reason_for_change: Normalize taxonomy and make the bounded mutation attributable and reversible without inventing persistence requirements.

new_technical_evidence.title: NVIDIA System Management Interface documentation - power limits and device selection
new_technical_evidence.applicability: nvidia-smi device identifiers and GPU/module power-limit semantics
new_technical_evidence.supports: UUID/BDF is preferred over unstable index; requested, enforced, default, minimum and maximum limits are distinct; supported products can expose module versus GPU power scopes.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Exact installed driver syntax/scope and platform-approved watts must be checked on the DUT.

removed_ambiguities: Binds value to stable target and explicit scope.
Separates requested/enforced readback and immediate save from persistence.
resolved_blockers: Missing watts/approval are resolvable prerequisites, not inherent BLOCKED.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 replaces the invalid `USER CONFIRMATION` label, prevents index/scope misapplication on newer power models, and limits acceptance to immediate requested/enforced readback plus exact restoration rather than an undefined persistence claim.

agent_understanding_result.notes: Initial validation found ambiguous five-minute semantics and no requested-versus-enforced acceptance rule. After revision, revalidation confirmed five minutes is planning metadata and the signed relationship/tolerance gates set, evidence, acceptance and restoration.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Compatibility row 301 sets an unspecified NVIDIA power limit and reads it back within five minutes.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 safety is strong but classification is noncanonical and power scope/persistence are underspecified.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Read-only range/pre-state collection is allowed; mutation requires exact tuple and restoration approval.
